collector.members: evaluatedAt, and each value of a query of the kind instant
collector.source: the clock of the telemetry collector

read.source: the wall clock of the host that ran the collector script

doesNotEstablish: That a caller obtained a completion at any instant. A scrape that succeeded, a request counter, and an error counter are what the telemetry collector stored. None of them is a request that a caller sent and had answered.
That a reading with the result no-series is a value of zero. No series is not zero, not healthy, and not failed.
That the telemetry collector existed or answered at a sample whose read state is not answered. A read that did not answer is not a result with no series.
That a metric means what its name says. A scrape that succeeded does not show that a counter agrees with what callers observed.
The instant of a change. A change is bounded by two scrapes of the collector and by two readings.
The resource use of the serving runtime, of a container, or of a node.
A rate, a ratio, a detection lag, or any other metric of an experiment. A stream is evidence that an analysis reads. This module computes no metric and gives no verdict.
limitations: The instants read.startedAt and read.finishedAt are the wall clock of the host that ran the collector script, in UTC, to one millisecond. A wall clock can be set while a collection runs. The end line names each reading whose start is before the finish of the reading before it.

A value is the answer of the telemetry collector to one instant query. It is not a reading of the process that published the metric. The collector answers from the last sample that it stored. That sample can be older than the read by the scrape interval. When the collector stored no newer sample and no mark that the series ended, the sample can be older by up to the lookback of the collector, which the chart leaves at the default of the collector. No run observed either.
The instant evaluatedAt and the value of a query of the kind instant are on the clock of the telemetry collector, to one millisecond. They are not on the clock of the collecting host.

The difference between the two clocks is not measured. The end line states two bounds that the evaluation instants give. The bounds hold when the collector took each evaluation instant while its read was open, and when the difference did not change during the collection. Each instant is cut to one millisecond, so each bound is to about one millisecond. No run observed when a collector takes the instant.

A reading with the result no-series states that the collector held no sample for the query at the evaluation instant. It does not state why. A metric that no process publishes, a target that the collector did not discover, and a sample that went stale each give no series.
A value of a counter is the sum over the processes that the collector scraped. The sum falls when a process starts again and when a target leaves. A stream computes no rate and corrects no reset.
The queries of one sample are separate reads at separate instants. They are not one atomic reading.
A state that began and ended between two scrapes is in no sample of the collector. A state that began and ended between two readings is in no reading.

Each kubectl call of a read states a request timeout, and kubectl applies it to each request that the call makes. The call of the Service read can make more than one request. No run observed how long a read takes. A query that the collector refused and a query that the API server could not pass to the collector are both unanswered.

A read reaches the collector through the Service proxy of the API server. The network policy of the chart selects the pod of the collector and admits no connection to its port. Whether a cluster applies that policy to a connection from the API server is a property of its network plugin. No run observed it.
The series of the collector are in a volume that goes when its pod goes. A stream holds only what was read while the collection ran.

The resources stream reads what the API process publishes about itself. No query reads the resource use of the serving runtime, of a container, or of a node, because the release has no source for them.
The chart renders the scrape job of the serving runtime only under the profile real. Under another profile the three queries of the serving runtime tier have no series.
A value of a registered label is free within the form of a label value. The form is not a check for a secret, and it does not show that the value is a registered outcome or a canonical error code.
A value of the kind number is stored as a binary number of 64 bits. A counter above 9007199254740992 loses its last digits.
A reading whose answer holds more than 32 series states no series.

The collection names the commit of the working tree that ran the collector script, and the SHA-256 of the script and of its library. It does not state whether the tree had a change that was not committed.
omitted: Each label of a series that the query does not register. Each registered query aggregates over every other label.
The name of a pod, of a scrape target, and of a scrape job, and the address of a target.
Each request identifier, correlation identifier, trace identifier, and tenant identifier. The telemetry catalog bars each from a metric label, and no registered query groups by one.
The text of an error that the collector or the API server returned.
The name of the kubeconfig context. A context name can hold an account identifier.
The Service object of the collector. The tool reads whether it is present and nothing else.

queries.name: api-processes-reporting-cpu
queries.states: The number of API processes whose processor time the collector holds.

queries.name: api-cpu-seconds
queries.states: The processor time of the API processes, in seconds, summed.

queries.name: api-resident-memory-bytes
queries.states: The resident memory of the API processes, in bytes, summed.
